hook.text: Money Illusion: a simple choice shows how real behavior departs from strict rationality.

buildup.text: Money illusion: people think in nominal terms (the dollar amount) rather than real terms (what the dollars can buy).

discovery.text: Fisher identified this in 1928. Nearly a century later, people still confuse higher numbers with greater wealth.

twist.text: Housing prices doubled in 20 years. After inflation, the gain is much less.

climax.text: Always convert to real terms. 'Am I buying more than before?' is the only question that matters for financial progress.

punchline.text: Big numbers aren't big wealth. Adjust for inflation.

quiz.question: What is money illusion?
options: Thinking in nominal terms rather than real purchasing power
